+---

+title: Make the timed test scenarios safe under machine load
+---
+## What
+Some unit tests race a wall clock. Under a high load average (55 to 170) the full `swift test` run fails some of them, and the failure set changes from run to run. Card ^vg37780 saw this (3 runs, no code change: 9 failing tests, then 2, then 0).
+
+- `Tests/Support/MCPTestServer/DynamicToolsetScenario.swift`: `startDynamicToolsetScenario()` fires its stages on 1.5 s timers (`scheduleMutation(after:)`). A test that reads the "first" catalog after more than 1.5 s sees the stage-1 tool. Affected: `ServerModeTests` ".dynamic registers the initial re-schemad tool up front", `RegistryRebuildTests` "rebuildRegistry() after the scenario adds a tool...", `SurfaceRefresherTests` (add and remove tests), `LiveCatalogTests.dynamicToolsetScenarioEmitsOneSnapshotPerStage`.
+- `ShellRunnerTests`: canceler tests poll `ps` for the spawned tree within `treeStartDeadline`; the time-limit test asserts `elapsed < timeoutUpperBound`.
+- `ProviderFallbackTests` "a timeout skips the provider with one note" and `ResilienceTests.freshOperationWaitsForInFlightDisconnectStragglerBoundedByDisconnectGracePeriod`.
+
+## Approach
+Let the test drive each stage with an explicit trigger (or an injected clock) in place of a wall-clock timer. Do not widen deadlines. Do not add retries.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] No listed test depends on a wall-clock race to pass.
+- [ ] The listed suites pass under a high load average.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Research done. Causes and plan for each race:
+    - DynamicToolsetScenario: three stages on 1.5 s timers. Plan: `startDynamicToolsetScenario()` registers the first tool only. New `advanceDynamicToolsetScenario()` runs the next stage on command. New `runDynamicToolsetStages(on:)` runs the stages on an injected clock; `ServerMode.dynamic` uses it with `ContinuousClock` by default, so `mcp-test-server --mode dynamic` keeps its timer. Tests advance each stage and wait for its snapshot before the next stage.
+    - ShellRunnerTests: the timeout timer sleeps on `Task.sleep`, and the tests poll `pgrep` within 2 s. Plan: inject `clock` into `ShellRunner` for the timer. A new test `GatedClock` holds each sleep until the test opens it. The tree commands print a ready line after the fork, and the test waits for that line on `outputChunkStream` (an event, not a deadline). The time-limit test uses the FIFO-gated command, so only the kill can end it.
+    - ProviderFallbackTests timeout: the 0.2 s policy is the limit of the SECOND provider too, and under load its instant answer loses to 0.2 s. Plan: the first provider fails with `URLError.timedOut` under the default policy. `WebFetcherTests.hangingRequestTimesOut` still covers the hang timer.
+    - ResilienceTests disconnect straggler: the client queue bounds its waits with `Task.sleep`. Plan: an internal `clientQueueClock` seam on `MCPServer` (internal init, public init forwards with `ContinuousClock`). The test opens a `GatedClock`, and reads `recordedSleeps` to prove the short bound.

+- actor: claude-code

+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed. What changed:
+    - New test clock `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/Support/GatedClock.swift`: each sleep waits until the test calls `open()`, then every sleep ends at once. It records each requested duration and obeys task cancellation.
+    - Dynamic scenario: `startDynamicToolsetScenario()` registers the first tool only. `advanceDynamicToolsetScenario()` runs one stage on command (returns `false` after the third). `runDynamicToolsetStages(on:)` runs the stages on a clock. `ServerMode.registerTools(on:stageClock:)` uses it, default `ContinuousClock`, so `mcp-test-server --mode dynamic` keeps its timer. LiveCatalog, RegistryRebuild and SurfaceRefresher tests advance each stage and wait for its snapshot or rebuild before the next stage. New tests: ScriptedServerSelf (one stage per advance), ServerMode (stages run on the stage clock).
+    - ShellRunner: new `var clock` (default `ContinuousClock`); the time-limit timer sleeps on it. Tree commands print `ready` after the fork, and the tests wait for that line on `outputChunkStream` (an event of the run, not a deadline). The time-limit test runs the FIFO-gated command, so only the kill can end it, and checks `recordedSleeps == [shortTimeout]`. `treeStartDeadline` and `timeoutUpperBound` are gone.
+    - ProviderFallback timeout: the first provider fails with `URLError.timedOut` under a 10 s policy. The old 0.2 s policy also limited the second provider, and under load its answer lost to that limit. `WebFetcherTests.hangingRequestTimesOut` still covers the hang timer.
+    - MCPServer: new internal `clientQueueClock` and an internal designated init. The public init forwards with `ContinuousClock`. `awaitWithBoundedWait(_:timeout:on:)` sleeps on it. The resilience test waits on `clientQueueTail` changes (events), opens a `GatedClock`, holds the fresh transport at a `GatedConnectTransport` so `.ready` comes after `.disconnected`, and reads `recordedSleeps` to prove the short bound.
+    Not changed, and why: the survivor polls of ShellRunnerTests (`treeExitDeadline`, 5 s) wait for process death after SIGKILL. That is a hang bound on an event, not on spawn latency, and the card does not list it. Note: I edited one doc line of `MCPServer+ClientQueue.swift` with `sed` by mistake; the content is correct.
